label: bram-kit
decisions: Kiln Vent: the cone angle is not stated, so it uses the cone primitive's default 90 degrees (as SPL-010 does). Its push is hostile displacement, which is hard control (L116), so it always shows the 0.25 s cue (L96). Control immunity blocks the push but not the 28 damage. A frontal guard halves it like any direct cone hit (L104).

Kiln Vent 'Heat strength 1 to affected world props' means one instant heat unit on the cells under each prop inside the cone. The cone itself deposits nothing and makes no field. Steam from heating a wet cell under a prop is an ordinary reaction, not a fire field.
Signatures have no grammar puzzle (L472), so Kiln Vent never gets the crest reward.

Tempered Hands is a DamageTaken effect filtered to the thermal channel with an 8 s internal cooldown. The shield arrives after the triggering hit (it never absorbs that hit), lasts 2 s and shares the 100 shield cap. Bram's own thermal damage does not trigger it, and reaction or other secondary damage raises no triggers (L126, L672).
Kiln Vent and Tempered Hands have no catalogue IDs of their own, so their tests carry [Verifies("WIZ-002")]. Their prose numbers are checked against the record's signature and passive text (D-011).

Only three exclusive groups exist in the catalogue: SPL-009-delivery (AUG-305/306), SPL-010-delivery (307/308) and SPL-014-delivery (315/316). The other transformation pairs have no group and may be owned together, which is tested in Economy.

Structural deltas: AUG-307 adds field to SPL-010, AUG-310 adds cone to SPL-011, AUG-316 adds trap and field to SPL-014, AUG-317 removes burn from SPL-015. The other twelve keep their base tags. Economy's profile and the Sim's resolved form agree on these (tested at both ranks).
AUG-318 Lash Steam 'wind-clear': a strength-2 gust disperses the front 2 m slice it touches (D-023), which removes the whole 1-1.5 m strip.

Bot crest attempts are a chance per competence: Novice 0, Apprentice 0.15, Adept 0.5, Expert 0.8 with the default profiles. Normal releases therefore commit reliably and mastery is occasional. A Novice's timing jitter can still land in the crest window by accident; that behavior is unchanged from CrestReleaseScript.

Spell interpretations from the earlier attempt are kept and listed in docs/notes/kit-wiz-002.md. Heat Haze reduces spell projectile damage only, inside the 45% cap. Ash Curtain is an ash volume counted as a field. Boiler Orb is a deployable with no field allocation, and water steams its heat at once. Flame Lash's Heat 1 ignites growth that already holds a heat unit (L153 threshold). Flashforge heats the nearest intact metal prop and counts it as one field, and it burns its owner too.

Premature recast (SPL-014/AUG-306/AUG-315), confirmed. A recast press while the cast's target does not exist yet (orb flying or falling, AUG-306 fireball before it plants the cinder, AUG-310 reservoir not yet charged) is now refused as NoPendingRecast. It spends no recast use and no surcharge (L94). Casts with no awaiting entity behave as before. AUG-310 is back on RecastRule.Default, and the old RecastAllowance=32 workaround is removed.

AUG-309, confirmed. Interpretation: 'steam also hides caster's view' means that while the caster's eye is inside his own mantle puff, he cannot acquire a target whose chest is outside it. This is stricter than L167 and never looser. A target inside the same puff stays visible ('close range'). Outside viewers keep the plain L167 rule: rank 2 hides Bram both ways, and at rank 1 the puff screens him once he steps behind it.

AUG-310: both reviewers' findings confirmed, and they conflicted. Interpretation: 'absorbed damage' is the damage the caster takes (shield + health) from hostile hits that the shimmer's projectile reduction acts on (ConditionalPrevented > 0). Melee, bursts, terrain, statuses and self damage never count. One catalogue Fireball (42.24 dealt) fills the reservoir; one 15-damage projectile (13.2) does not, and two do. The contradicting doc comments are fixed.

WIZ-002 crest scope: the inconsistency is confirmed. I resolved it with an explicit interpretation for the hub instead of a per-spell change, centralised in KitSupport.PrimaryBurstMastery and written up in the notes. The bonus goes to the primary payload: its direct amount where it has one (Fireball's alternative 28 splash is unchanged, now tested). Where the record's only damage is an area burst (Boiler Orb and the AUG-315/316 bursts, Phoenix Rush endpoint and AUG-314 brake), that burst counts as primary (L480 excludes only secondary/reaction damage; L478 gives every cast one benefit). Secondary damage (AUG-306 cinder burst, tested at generation 1 with no bonus) and terrain contact never get it.

Codex classification, AUG-312 first-tick push, SPL-016 marker point and the AUG-314/315/320 counterplay scenarios: already fixed and tested in earlier WIP commits on this branch (551c745, b3305c0, dbf0b3a, 9b503aa, b89dc10). I re-checked them: the generation-1 and Environment flags are in place, and EffectSystem.TranslateDamage skips them.

SPL-015 curved arc: earlier commits implement it as a swept strike (L102) of the lash's 0.5 m width across the light-blade arc, with the tip tracing the curve. Targets inside the swept sector are struck. This is recorded as an interpretation in the notes.
gaps: The full Confluence.sln test run had not finished when this report was due; re-run `dotnet test Confluence.sln` to confirm Casting, Hosting and the other projects pass.
Hub decisions needed (written up in docs/notes/kit-wiz-002.md): the crest reward on area-only primary payloads, the AUG-310 soak rule, the AUG-309 caster-view veil, and the recast-gate primitive.

label: halen-kit
decisions: Kit-wide interpretations from the earlier session are listed in docs/notes/kit-wiz-010.md. Examples: impact water without a stated duration lasts 3 s; Bubble Buckler protects a 50-degree half arc and a heat hit costs 10 shield and makes a 1 m puff; 'moving with its arrow' means grounded, in the stream's liquid water, at 0.5 m/s or more, within 45 degrees of the arrow; Deepglass Prison's slow starts when the root ends, or at once if immunity refused the root.

AUG-445 rolling bubble: the wall check sweeps level at the higher of the current and next ground height, so it climbs rises within the step height and rolls off drops. A face it is leaving never stops it. A 1 m crate stops it; a flying bubble passes over the same crate.
AUG-441: the landing puddle's 3 s / 4 s lifetime is counted from the landing tick; the launch water keeps its own 3 s.

AUG-443: the two lanes meet at the aimed point, 30 degrees either side of the aim, and each is its own field. 'Water 2 shared' means Water 1 per lane. A body gets +10% from at most one lane, and the straight-ahead line of the unforked stream is dry.
AUG-444 rank 2: the recast turns the arrow to whichever of reverse, left 90 or right 90 is closest to the caster's aim at that moment.
AUG-447: the record gives no cone angle, so the framework default of 90 degrees applies. 'Original focused removal 2 becomes 1' means at most 1 unit per cell, heat before venom.
AUG-448: corrosion is removed only when the same neutralization also removes heat (drawback 'unless actual neutralization').

Bot profile: spells are chosen by range and situation in this order: buckler against a visible windup, seal hazards near the feet, a pool on heat near the opponent as a steam screen, signature within 2.2 m, hammer within 3.2 m, prison at 5-17 m (60%), jet at 2.5-19 m, riptide or vault to close distance, pool at the opponent's feet. Mastery attempt chance by competence: Novice 0, Apprentice 15%, Adept 50%, Expert 75%. A 2-mana margin is kept above each cost.
End-to-end Seal the Spring duel: Fireball's Heat 2 is used up at impact and leaves no lasting hot ground, so that test places Bram's hot field directly in the reaction world.

AUG-447 (confirmed): the Spring Fan cone keeps SPL-080's 'one visible hot/corrosive ground field' rule, because L541 says a branch keeps what it does not replace. A cone cell counts only when the caster's eye has clear sight (DuelWorld.HasClearSight: no sight-blocking solid and less than the L167 obscuring limit) to the cell's surface point, which is the same SpringSight.SeenByCaster check the base splash uses. Heat behind a wall is untouched.

AUG-444 (confirmed): reaction cells pool all units of a material in one slot, so the world cannot say who owns which water. At release, LaneWaterLayer records per lane and per cell what the lane actually adds, using the L163 four-unit cap rule: min(strength, 4 - water already there). A shared fork junction cell is counted only once. On the rank-2 turn, only min(recorded, current water) is removed from each cell. Foreign water, and water the cap stopped the lane from adding, stays. The blanket footprint RemoveWater overload was deleted.

AUG-436 (confirmed): the impact-spot spray now works for any SPL-074 delivery (new WaterHammerScript.StrikeReach). The cone's impact spot is where its center line from the focus meets a solid within the 3 m reach. The miss recovery is unchanged.

AUG-435/441/446 structure (confirmed; the claude-verifier and codex findings overlap): the earlier round made these puddles owned gameplay fields (TidePuddleEntity, three-field allocation, oldest retired). To match that, HalenStructure now registers a 'field' delta for AUG-435 (SPL-074), AUG-441 (SPL-077) and AUG-446 (SPL-079), per L543 and in line with SPL-076. Clouds, puffs and mist are still treated as reaction byproducts and carry no tag. The table-driven record and Economy profile tests cover the new rows.

Codex SPL-080, AUG-437, the puddle cap and bot aiming: I re-checked each one and found it already fixed by the earlier WIP commits on this branch (a1c97eb splash sight and a test with a field hidden behind a wall; d9975a7 recast rejected after a break, with a DuelWorld test; eaef86f owned puddle fields; 4dca945 the bot holds its planned ground aim until the spell releases, with a BotInputSource-to-DuelWorld test). label: augments-a
decisions: 'Preparation decreases X%' and 'longer preparation' (AUG-055, 065, 066) mean the windup after commitment, following AUG-005.
Field records: a field is a FieldDelivery (circle, lane or rectangle). 'Radius' is a circle's radius or a lane's half-width. 'Initial direct damage' is the first-contact (enter) payload.

Field placement conditions (distance, overlap, overhead cover) are judged at commitment, from FieldDelivery.PredictTarget along the current aim. Fields of either player and player clouds count as 'another field'.
'Exactly one living persistent field' (AUG-068) counts the owner's field entities, spell fields and clouds both.
'Direct player damage decreases 2%' (AUG-059, 125) applies only to the owner's direct spell hits on players. 'Airborne-target damage' (AUG-030) is the owner's spell hits on an airborne target.
'Enemy-created cover' (AUG-059) is any destructible solid the opponent created.
'Cover object' (AUG-067) is any destructible solid. A 'dry destructible' (AUG-125) is a prop whose cell has no liquid water.
'Heat effect' (AUG-125) means school Heat, a heat tag, or the thermal channel.
AUG-059 and AUG-067 record a 'my spell's direct impact hit solid X' fact inside AdjustSolidDamage, because SolidEvent carries no source. The returned amount stays a pure function of the inputs.
AUG-062 'within 4 m' is the horizontal distance from the owner's feet to the prop's base center.

AUG-105: the lateral motion is a 0.1 s self displacement after takeoff (motor collision, legal boundary). The jump's horizontal velocity is restored afterwards, so exactly the stated distance is added and the jump gains no height. It emits an owner 'wall-exit' cue.
AUG-082: a second weapon hit inside the 1 s window cancels the setup. The projectile must be released inside that 1 s.
AUG-088 'within 2 m of solid cover' means a vertical solid face within 2 m. AugmentsAKit.NearVerticalSolid probes 16 waist-height rays; AUG-105 uses the same probe.

AUG-006 'stationary' is grounded, undisplaced and below 0.1 m/s. AUG-103 'walking sideways' means more of the horizontal velocity runs across the facing than along it. AUG-103 charges +1 mana if preparation began, or payment happens, while sprinting.

Mastery-linked bonuses clamp with the grammar reward (L480): damage and speed at 15% via CastFacts; mastered-only cost reductions are efficiency and now clamp with a mana reward at 20% (MasteryClamp.RewardedCastEfficiency).
AUG-070: the range bonus applies to aimed field forms with range at least 10 m. The lifetime drawback applies to every owner field, with a 1 s minimum.
AUG-117: the stamina saving is spread over the first 30 ticks of a sprint begun with the cooldown ready. The 5 s cooldown starts at that sprint.
Records whose draft requirement is equipment, a feat or another augment do not re-check that requirement in the duel. Economy eligibility and dormancy (L602-L646) decide when they are active.

Mastery-linked = every Casting mastery family record (all tagged 'mastery'). Their direct-damage and projectile-speed bonuses (AUG-001, 006, 007, 009, 013, 018, 020) are reported through EffectHook.LinkedDirectDamage / LinkedProjectileSpeed, summed per cast, and clamped once with the cast's own reward at 15% (L480). Speed changes that are not mastery-linked (AUG-025/026/103) stay outside that clamp.

One reward per cast (AUG-005/014/020 finding, rated plausible): kept the cross-category reading and did not change the code. L124 'never both' limits the grammar reward itself. L480 says 'Different statistical categories still obey the full combat caps'. The strict reading would make AUG-005 do nothing for all ten wizards it lists, because none of them has a windup reward. This is documented in MasteryClamp.RewardedCastEfficiency and the notes. The hub may want a DECISIONS entry.

Gait: hooks request signed walk/sprint changes through AdjustGait. The host sums them; bonuses join the stat gait bonus under the +20% cap; penalties apply after the cap, so a drawback is never absorbed by it. Only the change is applied on top of the command's multipliers, so other edits to the command survive.

AUG-109 Wet Route unmarked. Spec L175 and the Water Pool record ('no automatic slow') give shallow water no movement penalty, so the record has nothing to reduce. The earlier version reduced any slow on a wet surface, enemy spell slows included, which the record never states.

AUG-031: 'release at least 1 m above enemy feet' = the caster's feet are at least 1 m above the enemy's feet at release (a ledge, or near the 1.1 m jump apex). Measured from the eye, every level-ground release qualified.
AUG-043 trail and AUG-105 exit are a new public MarkerEvent with From/To/Direction/DurationTicks. It is an authoritative event both clients receive and has no rule effect or collision.
AUG-012 is judged at release (L90-L92). The 2/4 mana comes back through the cast's refund ledger, like the other conditions that complete after commitment.
AUG-080 'paid spell within 0.5 s' = the commitment (payment, L90) must fall within 0.5 s of the perfect guard. A WIZ-002 tap fits after the guard's release window.
AUG-082: a projectile that hits on its release tick is boosted when the record's own 0.5 s proc interval is open. The activation is still recorded once, at the dispatch point.

Field placement prices (AUG-053, 054, 060, 065, 066) settle against the field actually created (FieldSettlementHook). Drawbacks are charged at commitment from the predicted placement, then returned or charged after the fact at creation; an after-the-fact charge never takes more mana than the caster has. Decreases come back through the refund ledger (25% cap) once the created field qualifies. AUG-065/066 also set the windup from the placement, so an aimed field is created at the committed ground point and direction (BindFieldPlacement). Fields centred on the caster are not bound, though their price still settles.
Field placement distance is measured from the caster's feet to the placement point: the centre of a circle or rectangle, the start of a lane.
gaps: AUG-109 Wet Route: unmarked; its class and tests were removed. It needs a rules-side shallow-water movement penalty (or a DECISIONS entry defining one) before the record has anything to reduce.

Field-requirement records (AUG-049..055, 060, 065, 066, 068, 070) are verified in DuelWorld with test field behaviours (ShapedField) registered under SPL-012/SPL-013. Real catalogue ids are needed because CatalogueLoadouts takes mana, range and windup from the catalogue. Multi-spell records (AUG-020, 041, 082, the stacking tests) likewise use TestBolt under SPL-014/015/016/073.

AUG-065/066: for fields centred on the caster, the windup part is decided at commitment and is not bound to that position (only the price settles at creation). Walking under or out of cover during the windup keeps the windup chosen at commitment. AUG-066's 0.05 s outdoor drawback cannot be added after release if cover is destroyed during the windup.
After-the-fact drawback charges (field settlement) take at most the mana the caster has (L78), so a caster at 0 mana can leave such a drawback unpaid.

label: net-protocol
decisions: Incremental cell capture is exact by a Reactions invariant: every non-empty cell is active (Cell.IsActive), and the active list is rebuilt at the end of every step. So refreshing the active cells plus the cells reported last time reproduces the full scan. A full safety scan still runs on the first capture and every 30 captures. No Reactions edit was needed (ReactionWorld.ActiveCells already exists).
The 150 ms rewind (L423) covers the whole stepTick-viewTick distance, interpolation included. Shots are fully favored up to about 60-70 ms RTT and clamped beyond that.
The interpolation delay adapts between 50 and 250 ms; 'about 100 ms' is treated as the typical value, not a cap.
Opponent health is never sent during a duel. Damage amounts go only to the attacker and the target. Results show both health fractions afterwards (L49).
Live duelists get other pairs' results and standings only after their own duel ends or after 15 s (L391).
Invisible opponents beyond the 4 m silhouette are culled on the server, with an early reveal margin of 1 m plus 0.25 s of closing speed.
D-115's 5% loss threshold is measured as snapshot loss over a sliding 4 s window.
Input timing tuning: queue target 1 tick; surplus cut above 4 ticks after 0.5 s; input rate limit burst 32 then 1 per 8 ms; kick after 2000 rate-limited or faulting messages.
Grammar events may be back-dated 1 tick for taps, traces, widgets and stroke ends, and 9 ticks (the rewind bound) for syllables and stroke samples.
Standard matches use a cryptographic random seed. --seed needs --lab or --allow-fixed-seed.
A client that cannot regenerate an arena exactly downloads the server's layout. Only a failed download shows the unsupported-version state (L427).

Real-time pacing is needed to measure reliable-lane latency in tests, because LiteNetLib times its reliable resends by wall clock. The accelerated rig cannot measure it, so I added GameRig.PaceRealTime.

Hidden opponent (L120): the live pose is replicated exactly when DuelWorld.IsVisibleTo is true. The 1 m plus closing-speed early-reveal margin is gone, so no coordinates are sent beyond 4 m. The client never interpolates between a frozen hidden pose and a live one.

DuelEventFilter.Conceal: for an opponent hidden from the viewer, cast and movement events always lose position and direction. Every event the hidden player acts in loses its direction. Events it acts in, takes damage in, or is targeted by lose any position within 3 m of its live position. Reaction cues its own effects cause within 3 m are dropped. Neutral terrain reactions and far positions stay (L120).
Owner-attached entities (Movement, Buff, Other) carry the origin as position and are drawn on the owner's replicated pose. A hidden owner's attached entities are left out of the viewer's frame.

View-claim validation: the declared interpolation is clamped to the honest 3-15 ticks, slewed at 1 tick per 20 arrival ticks per session, and capped at InterpolationCeiling = one-way + min(jitter, 3) + snapshot interval + 2. The jitter widening of the tolerance is capped at 3 ticks. Metrics gain interpolationLimited and a claimed-minus-expected histogram (viewOffsets, -8..+8).

Results (L49 'fast winners ... through delayed information', L391): a result goes to its two duelists at once. Every other seat, fighting or not, gets it when it is 15 s old, when no duel of the pass is live, or at match end. The same rule (MayKnow) applies on the normal, deferred and reconnect paths.

Reviewer claim checked and partly not confirmed: standings change only in MatchFlow.ResolvePass, when no duel is live, so CatchUp's StandingsNow never leaked a live pair's fresh outcome. For consistency, a live duelist that reconnects now gets the standings last released to it, and current standings after its duel or the delay.

Reconnect: per seat the server keeps the released results, the seat's own reports and the last standings, and CatchUp replays them. A seat resuming after the match finished gets settings, final standings, every result, its reports and MatchEnd (CatchUpFinished). The client keeps one result and one report per duel id, and raises MatchEnded once.

A tapped button (pressed and released inside one command) is a press edge for every action (melee, guard, jump, dodge, swap) in DuelWorld.ApplyInput, as it already was for casting. A tap of a button held before or now is no new press. MotorPredictor.PressedEdges mirrors it.

Production transports (GameTransport.Defaults, the server CLI and the headless CLI) run LiteNetLib threads (ManualMode=false) to mitigate #616 until a fixed release is pinned. --manual-transport opts back in; --threaded-transport is still accepted. Virtual-clock tests keep manual mode.
The accelerated pace is at most x16 (NetRules.MaxTickRate 1000, the rate Welcome and match settings can decode). GameServer refuses a faster pace and the CLI limits --accelerated to 1-16.

Wizard choices freeze once the MatchHost exists (the arena warm-up). A join with another wizard is refused with MatchRunning; an identical re-join is accepted. A seat whose session expires during the warm-up is no longer freed.

The client holds snapshots, events and reports of a duel whose DuelStart has not arrived yet (up to 512 messages, by duel id) and applies them when it arrives. An authoritative Ended snapshot ends the client duel.
The private entry carries RecallEndTick, which needed a wire change (NetRules.ProtocolVersion 3). The predicted motor holds while tick < RecallEndTick, as DuelWorld step 2 does.
Metrics: a record for every live duel flushed at shutdown, plus one session-summary JSON line per human seat at match end or shutdown.

HMAC finding: I did not withhold the arena recipe seed. The arena seed is also public in the arena id ('arena:rN.aM:<seed hex>') and in the layout's seed field, which the layout hash covers, so withholding only the recipe would not close the leak. This is recorded as an open blocker instead.
